title: Add drift-aware hotspot detector and sequence-phase sampler for representative workload runs
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Current workload runners assume stationary request mixes; production traces show long-term drift and recurring short-term phases (e.g., bursts of short prompts vs. long-context completions). This PR introduces a drift-aware hotspot detector and a sequence-phase sampler that: 1) identifies stable phases in a sequence of requests, 2) detects gradual distribution drift, and 3) emits representative subpopulations for downstream perf benchmarks and profiling.

Design summary: The detector uses an online two-tier approach: a lightweight sketch (histogram + EWMA of sequence length and token mix) for real-time drift flags, and a phase segmentation step using a HMM-inspired run-length model to find coherent phase windows. The sampler prioritizes phase coverage and tail events while respecting a target token budget. Output artifacts include per-phase flamegraphs, KV-cache warmup profiles, and a "phase-coverage" manifest used by the perf harness to seed sessions.

Changes included: new runner module (bench_driftsampler/), a phase visualization exporter (reports/phase-coverage/), CLI flags to the runner (--phase-sample-rate, --drift-threshold), integration hooks with the existing kv-warmup simulator, and unit + regression tests.

How to run: ./tools/bench-runner --repo traces/ --profile drift --phase-sample-rate 0.2 --out reports/phase-coverage/

Compatibility: Backwards-compatible with existing workload descriptors. When phase sampling is disabled the runner falls back to previous random sampling mode.

Test plan: Local unit tests (bench_driftsampler/*) + integration smoke runs on synthetic traces. Performance regression suite ran on k80-small and p4d-sim with no >3% p95 increases; KV-cache warmup improved steady-state token savings for mixed workloads by ~6%.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for detector and sampler
- [x] Integration with kv-warmup simulator
- [x] Small-scale perf run and baseline comparison
- [x] Documentation for new CLI flags and reporter
- [x] Added Linear tickets (ENG-3412, ENG-3499)

Context links: Linear ENG-3412 (phase-sampling initiative), internal trace dump used for analysis: s3://redwood-bench/traces/2024-09-drift-sample

@@ def detect_phase(seq_lengths):
-    if not seq_lengths: return []
+    # use adaptive run-length segmentation to find stable windows
+    if not seq_lengths: return []
+    state_scores = _compute_run_scores(seq_lengths)
+    return _segment_runs(state_scores)

@@ def sample_sessions(manifest, budget):
-    return random.sample(manifest, k)
+    # prefer underrepresented phases and tail events to maximize coverage
+    by_phase = group_by(manifest, 'phase')
+    picks = _round_robin_phase_selection(by_phase, budget)
+    return picks
review_comments: Arjun Patel: Nice design. Two small requests: (1) make drift threshold configurable via env var for CI runs, (2) add a lightweight end-to-end smoke test that writes a phase manifest to tmpfs so we don't spam S3 in PR runs.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed both items: added DRIFT_THRESHOLD env and a smoke test that writes to /tmp (bench_driftsampler/tests/test_end_to_end_smoke.py). Updated docs with CI guidance.
Sofia Gomez: Could we instrument the per-phase KV-hit-rate in the flamegraph exporter? That helps correlate warmup to throughput improvements.
Maya Chen: Added kv_coverage metric and a simple histogram in reports/phase-coverage/visualizer.py. See commit b5412a0.
Liam O'Connor: Perf runs look stable. One nit: the HMM-style segmentation uses a fixed transition penalty; can we make that adaptive based on recent variance?
Maya Chen: Filed ENG-3499 to follow up with an adaptive penalty; kept default conservative for this PR to limit scope.

release_notes: Added a drift-aware hotspot detector and a sequence-phase sampler for generating representative benchmark sessions. New artifacts: per-phase flamegraphs, phase-coverage manifests, KV-cache coverage metrics. No breaking changes.
notes_for_release: Enable --phase-sample-rate in nightly perf runs to collect baseline phase coverage artifacts. ENG-3412/ENG-3499 for follow-ups (adaptive segmentation and scheduler tuning).
